cameraProjectionBand.description: The top-view band containing the visible rear loop halo.

rejectedExperiments.method: Fade family-1 and family-3 tails from normalized curve position 0.62.
rejectedExperiments.result: The loop halo remained because the dominant projected points are earlier in the curve.

rejectedExperiments.method: Ray-project the first five or six family-1 and family-3 points onto monotonic scalp routes.
rejectedExperiments.result: The halo remained, proving the root attachment segment was not the visible cause.

rejectedExperiments.method: Replace family-1 and family-3 middle points with a smooth outward arc.
rejectedExperiments.result: The random halo became a uniform comb-like wall and was visually worse.

conclusion: The rear halo is a structural projection of the current sheet-like families, concentrated around local points 7-10. Local smoothing cannot produce believable hair. Families 1 and 3 must be replaced by authored primary and secondary clumps with controlled spacing and overlap.
nextRequiredPass: Build a new low-count primary guide family, generate clustered children around each guide, and remove families 1 and 3 only after the replacement closes the rear silhouette and passes static and animated collision checks.
